title: Court enforceable undertakings
subject: This guide explains ASIC's approach to accepting court enforceable undertakings under the legislation it administers. It describes what a court enforceable undertaking is, how it works, and the circumstances in which ASIC will consider accepting one.
background: Court enforceable undertakings are an administrative remedy for contraventions of legislation administered by ASIC. The guide is intended for entities or persons and their legal advisers who are considering offering a court enforceable undertaking to ASIC. It is issued under the ASIC Act, National Credit Act, and SIS Act.
ruling: ASIC will consider accepting a court enforceable undertaking where it provides an effective regulatory outcome, such as remediation, compliance, or other corrective action. The undertaking must be clear, unambiguous, and capable of being enforced by a court. ASIC expects the undertaking to include acceptable and standard terms, and may require appointment of independent experts, public reporting, and compliance with the law. ASIC maintains a register of enforceable undertakings and will not accept undertakings that contain unacceptable terms or that are not in the public interest.
legislation_referenced: Australian Securities and Investments Commission Act 2001 (Cth) s 93A
